messages.subject: Make packrat more modular
parts:
Hi,

I like the whole idea of packrat a lot, but have repeatedly had problems in several ways. 

- A project directory contains code from R packages, that get searched by default when initializing. These days, I often copy the packrat directory from somewhere else because of this. 
- It cannot find a certain package - in this case SVGAnnotation. It is a bioconductor package that has no biocViews entry, so doesn't get detected as being from bioconductor. During installation, after potentitally 30 minutes of waiting while bioconductor re-installs, it just fails. Another restore then does everything over again
- Snapshotting is really slow
- In general, there is little fine-grained control over the process. 

I was wondering if the whole process could be made more modular, and certain sub-functionality exposed, mostly:

- Search a directory (not just the project directory, any one) recursively for R files and extract which packages are being called
- Given a list of packages, resolve the dependencies
- Given a list of packages with version numbers, download them. For this, look through several sources. For Bioconductor, also search several versions;
- Install the packages, but use only those downloaded; don't download anything else
- Given a library, return the list of packages (not just as available.packages, but e.g. with github information included).

I know that most of this functionality is already included in the package, but from reading the packrat sources I have trouble identifying which internal functions do exactly what. 

Is this something that is in scope/planned/you see as sensible?

Thanks!

Holger
